title: Internal Medicine in Vietnam, vol. II: General Medicine and Infectious Diseases (AMEDD official history)
citation: Andre J. Ognibene and O'Neill Barrett Jr., eds., Internal Medicine in Vietnam, vol. II, General Medicine and Infectious Diseases (Washington, D.C.: Office of The Surgeon General and Center of Military History, 1982), chapters 3, 14, and 18.
notes: Official Army Medical Department history. Chapter 14 records 462 falciparum-malaria patients admitted to the U.S. Army Hospital, Camp Zama between August and December 1965 (citing Reed, Feinstein & Steiger, JAMA 1968) — placing Vietnam disease evacuees at Camp Zama in exactly Larry's window. Chapter 18 covers hepatitis (dark urine, light stool). Chapter 3 documents the 1965 fifteen-day in-country evacuation policy.
